PullRequest.Title: copilot: fix shell argument injection in generated commit messages
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #316995
Fixes #316996

## The bug

`github.copilot.terminal.generateCommitMessage` types `git commit -m <message>` into the active terminal. It is the terminal quick fix offered after a successful `git add`. The old sanitizer escaped `"` before `\`, so its second `replace` re-escaped the backslash the first one had just added, and the message could end its own `-m` argument. Backticks were never escaped either, so command substitution still worked.

It is worse than typed-but-not-run. `Terminal.sendText` turns every line break into an Enter key press, and generated messages are usually multi-line. So a message that breaks out of its quotes **runs without the user pressing Enter**, even though the command is sent with `shouldExecute: false`.

## The fix

`buildGitCommitCommand` builds the command for the terminal's detected shell (`TerminalState.shell`):

| Terminal | Command |
|---|---|
| bash, zsh, sh, ksh, Git Bash | `-m '…'` with POSIX single quotes. The message is kept intact, line breaks included. |
| fish | `-m '…'`, with `\` and `'` escaped, because fish treats both as escapes inside single quotes. |
| PowerShell | `-m '…'`, doubling `'` and the typographic single quotes PowerShell also treats as delimiters (U+2018, U+2019, U+201A, U+201B). `"` becomes `'`, and a trailing `\` gets a space after it, which git's message cleanup removes again. Without this, Windows PowerShell 5.1's legacy native argument passing splits the argument at a `"` and lets a trailing `\` escape its closing quote. PowerShell 5.1 and 7 both report `pwsh`, so they can't be told apart. |
| cmd, nu, csh, WSL, other or undetected shells | One `-m "…"` per paragraph, reduced to characters every shell treats literally inside double quotes. `$`, `!` and `%` are removed; `"`, backticks and typographic quotes become `'`; `\` becomes `/`; the lines of a paragraph are joined. This is needed because cmd runs each line as soon as it's entered and expands `%VAR%` inside quotes, and the quoting rules of an unknown shell are unknown. |
| An agent CLI running in the terminal (Copilot CLI, Claude, Codex, Gemini and so on) | Nothing is typed, because the text would be a prompt to another agent. |

Control characters are removed for every shell, and a tab becomes a space. Typed control characters are commands to the shell's line editor. For example, a Backspace can erase the opening quote, and a following line break then runs the rest; that was reproduced in Git Bash and pwsh 7.6.

Agent Host terminals never report a shell type, so they always get the one-line form. That includes the Agents window, which has no Source Control view that a fallback could use.

The inline `// CodeQL [SM02383]` suppression is removed, since the double-escaping pattern it covered is gone.

## Validation

- **Unit tests:** 9 tests in `shellQuoting.spec.ts` (vitest).
- **Real shells:** every form was run through real shells into a native program and compared byte for byte. That covered Git Bash, pwsh 7.6, Windows PowerShell 5.1 and cmd.exe; the single-quote rules were also run through WSL bash, fish 4.9.3, and pwsh 7.6 in `Legacy` argument-passing mode. The inputs included the payloads from both issues and from review.
- **PowerShell parser:** the real parser in 5.1 and 7.6 read the single-quoted form of every BMP character, and of 20,000 random hostile strings, as a single literal equal to the input.
- **Interactive terminals:** real `git commit` commands were typed into interactive cmd, pwsh 7.6, Windows PowerShell 5.1 and Git Bash sessions through a pty, exactly as `sendText(text, false)` sends them. Nothing committed or ran before Enter, each produced exactly one commit, and `git log` showed the expected message.

## Known limitations

- The one-line form is lossy: the lines of a paragraph are joined, and `` `$var` `` becomes `'var'`. If Agent Host terminals reported a shell type, they could use the lossless forms instead.
- These predate this PR and are not injection paths:
  - Windows PowerShell 5.1 drops typed characters outside the console code page, such as `’`, `✓` and emoji. Git Bash turns a typed emoji into `�`.
  - Git Bash's MSYS runtime rewrites an argument that starts with `/` as a Windows path.
  - For remote Agent Host sessions the command does nothing, because `vscode.git` only opens `file:` repositories.

`copilotCLITerminalIntegration.ts` has a separate `quoteArgsForShell` for Copilot CLI paths and arguments. It is intentionally left unchanged here.

Scenarios.Scenario: User invokes the terminal “Generate Commit Message” quick fix after staging or modifying files, with a normal shell active.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Repository lookup and status refresh, per-change diff collection, recent Git history/config reads, prompt rendering, one model network request, linear command quoting, then terminal sendText must complete in sequence before the generated command appears. The new quoting work is on the critical path but is linear in the bounded generated message and negligible relative to unchanged Git/network work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the repository and refresh Git status through the VS Code Git extension API.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One repository lookup and status refresh per user invocation; no collection fan-out added by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same repository lookup and status refresh occurred before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before changes can be collected.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Collect diffs for changed files; tracked changes use Git repository diff calls, while untracked files use one stat and potentially one read per untracked file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Sequentially scales with the effective changed-file count after content-exclusion checks; unchanged by this diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The identical per-change diff path ran before command sanitization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All selected diffs complete before prompt generation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read up to five repository commits, user Git configuration, and up to five user commits.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two bounded log reads plus one or two config reads per invocation; unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same bounded Git metadata reads occurred before this PR.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send one rendered commit-message request to the Copilot utility model.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per command invocation, with no batching or cache in either version.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same single model request occurred before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Dominates latency and must complete before command construction.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Insert the constructed git command into the active terminal with sendText.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one terminal dispatch per successful invocation; agent shells and empty sanitized messages now dispatch zero.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Previously dispatched at most one command as well; the PR changes only quoting and suppresses dispatch for agent shells/empty results.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Final boundary that makes the command visible in the terminal.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Git/disk work scales sequentially with the number of changed files; model input scales with truncated diffs. The newly added helper scales linearly with generated-message characters and, for unknown shells, paragraph count. It is called once per explicit user action.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The scenario is serialized through awaited repository, diff, Git metadata, and network operations. Diff collection is sequential. The diff adds no limiter, queue, parallel loop, or concurrency burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Repository API state may already be warm, but status and generation are refreshed per invocation. The existing commit-message map tracks retries/survival rather than avoiding requests. The new quoting helper is stateless; cold and warm behavior are equivalent and it does not alter cache keys, misses, invalidation, or coalescing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: the full changed call site and helper were inspected, along with transitive Git diff, Git metadata, prompt, model-request, and terminal boundaries. The diff adds only synchronous string transformations before the existing terminal dispatch.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact Git and model durations vary with repository size and network conditions, but those costs and their cardinality are unchanged. Generated response length is endpoint-bounded in practice; even without relying on that bound, the new work is linear and performed once per explicit invocation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The helper replaces three linear string replacements with a small shell-dependent sequence of linear transformations once per generated message, without adding boundary calls, fan-out, retained state, or meaningful critical-path cost.

Scenarios.Scenario: User invokes the quick fix while an agent CLI is the active terminal shell.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The unchanged repository/Git/model generation path still completes, then the new helper detects the agent shell and returns without terminal dispatch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run the same repository status, diff, Git metadata, and one model request used for normal shells.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One generation workflow per explicit invocation; changed-file fan-out remains sequential and unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Before the PR, the same generation workflow ran and its result was sent to the terminal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These operations complete before shell suppression is evaluated.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Unchanged changed-file count and prompt size drive Git/model cost; the new agent-shell membership check is constant time.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One serialized invocation path; no new parallelism or coalescing behavior.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Same existing retry-tracking state and no generation cache. Shell suppression adds no cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: agent detection occurs in buildGitCommitCommand only after generateCommitMessage resolves.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The generation can be expensive, but that work is pre-existing rather than introduced or amplified by the diff.
Scenarios.Verdict: No diff-caused performance regression. Although generation is wasted for agent terminals, it was already performed before the PR; the change removes the final terminal IPC instead of adding work of comparable cost.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all three changed files and traced the user-triggered commit-message workflow through Git subprocess/IPC, filesystem reads, model network generation, quoting, and terminal dispatch. The only new production work is one stateless O(message length) shell-aware transformation per explicit invocation; it introduces no boundary fan-out, retained state, cache regression, concurrency burst, or synchronous UI hot-loop cost. No findings were submitted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
